content.thinking:
I'm planning the full build in one pass: a deer-like quadruped sized around 1.35m at the back with antlers reaching 1.9m, facing forward with a body length of roughly 1.5m. I'm settling on a jade, cream, and gold color palette for the design.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton -- hips as root, then spine, neck, head, jaw, and tail chains, each with specific joint positions and parent relationships to form the creature's structure.

Next I'm working out the leg geometry: front legs branching from shoulder joints down to hoof targets, using multi-segment limb chains with defined bend directions for the elbow and knee joints.

Building the leg geometry now, tapering radii from hip to hoof, and modeling the hooves as cloven two-toe boxes offset slightly from the leg's center line, positioned near ground level.

For the body, I'm lofting a series of stations from rump to chest along the spine bones, varying width and height to shape the torso naturally, then thinking through a coat paint using countershading and a cel-shaded approach.

For the neck, I'm tapering the tube radius from the chest up toward the head and applying a cream coloring on the forward-facing normal to mimic a pale throat, since the neck curves mostly upward and forward.

Now I'm moving on to building the head itself, positioning it at the top of the neck and working out skull and snout shapes using scaled spheres and frustum boxes placed along world axes rather than bone-local orientation.

Still working out eye decal placement and ear geometry...

Actually, simpler to avoid mirroring confusion entirely: I'll just define a fixed head world position and place all head parts using absolute world coordinates with offsets, rather than local bone-relative coordinates.

Mapping out the skull, snout, and antler positions as curved paths sweeping up from the skull, branching outward symmetrically on each side.

Adding more tine directions, then moving to the mane — I'll layer cloud-swirl textured cards along the neck's dorsal curve plus small puff spheres in cream and jade for volume.

Adding swirl decal cards with cream/jade variants leaning backward on the neck puffs, then doing similar cloud-puff clusters for the tail with positioned spheres and matching swirl decals near the final tail joint.

Generating the spiral path programmatically instead of hand-coding it, then assigning distinct darker shades for cream and jade swirl decals. For gold details, I'm thinking through a chest collar band as a girth loop around the body at the spine's chest point.

For the pendant, I'm placing a flattened jade disc with a gold torus ring and navy tassel cones, using a ray cast from in front of the chest to find where it actually touches the body surface so it sits correctly, skipping placement if no hit is found.

Now I'm working out gold flank swirl ornaments, extruding crescent outlines and orienting them using surface hits sampled around the body at specific angles on the flanks.

I'm checking that the scroll shape edges don't cross, then positioning it at the shoulder with a small thickness offset along x. Now I'm thinking about adding gold greaves as a short sweep around the lower legs.

For the gold cuffs, I'm planning to sweep a rod along a cropped portion of the leg chain's path, using a radius function based on the leg's radius plus a small offset, placing one near the fetlock and possibly another near the knee. Then I'm considering navy color bands for the lower leg portion.

Now I'm adding cream puff spheres at the hocks and elbows using the leg sweep's positioning function, placing small spherical tufts at symmetric angles along the leg, plus a smaller feather puff near the fetlock.

Next I'm working out the hip and tail geometry: positioning the hind leg root joint relative to the body, then building the tail as a chain of points curving up and back from the hips, tapering in radius with a cream puff at the tip.

Adding fur puffs along the tail...

I should also double-check that none of the tail puffs dip below ground level given the hoof positions.

Now working out the mane sweep along the neck tube, placing tufts at intervals with side variations, plus ear placement using tapered spikes angled outward and back with smaller inner ear details in salmon.

I'm adding whisker rods as curved sweeps from the snout sides in cream, and sketching a gold diamond accent on the forehead to sit above a jade brow ridge.

Now I'm placing a small gold octahedron on the forehead for the crest piece, adding dark nostril spheres at the snout tip, and planning the head's jade cel-shaded coloring with a cream fur edge around the cheeks.

For the head paint, I'm using a position-based fur edge so everything below y=1.665 shades cream for the muzzle underside and cheeks while the jade stays on top where the eyes sit — the snout naturally falls mostly in the cream zone this way. Next I'm working on the cloud neck textures, sketching a fluffy cloud shape from overlapping circles with a spiral accent.

Writing SVG code...

Now I'm positioning gold scroll ornaments along the horse's back, placing vertical scroll plates at the withers and rump so they protrude upward from the body's top surface.

I'll also add a jade medallion with tassels at the flanks—a torus ring in gold, a flattened jade sphere as the disc, and navy cone tassels with gold beads, mirrored on both sides.

For the gold chest band, I'm using a loop cut at a vertical plane through the body to create a girth ring, making sure it targets only the body loft surface and not the legs, then sweeping it with a small radius.

Now I'm setting up the coat with scattered color seeds across greenish tones and a darker base, and thinking about countershading—adding a cream belly where the surface normal points downward enough, possibly blending it with the same scale pattern technique.

Still defining leg colors and radius tapering...

Settling on a flat 0.058 cuff radius so it sits proud of the cannon by about a centimeter, then working out the hind leg segments similarly — hip to stifle to hock to fetlock with radii tapering from .12 down to .036, and placing the hind cuff around t=.74-.84 with radius .062.

For positioning, I'm mapping out z-coordinates for each foot target so the hind legs bend naturally with the hock trailing behind, and the front shoulder root sits forward near z=.38 with the foot further out at z=.42. I'm also double-checking the joint naming convention — four names per leg correspond to root, two intermediate joints, and the foot, giving a three-segment path per limb.

Now I'm working through the spine and neck chains: four spine points from hip to chest with names spine1-3 and chest, parented appropriately so the front legs attach to the chest tip joint and hind legs attach to the hips. Then I'm sketching the neck path rising from the chest point upward and forward toward the head, naming its joints.

Still working out skull and snout positioning...

Still placing facial details...

Now I'm setting up the antlers on the head bone, sweeping spike shapes along a path with gold coloring to form the beam structure.

Still placing facial details...

Adding more gold armor plates...

Still placing mane puffs...

Now I'm adding chin and chest cream tufts along the neck's front/belly side, with cards angled downward for a drooping flow, then moving on to fetlock and elbow puffs on each leg using sweep positions near the joints.

For the legs, I'm figuring out which side is front vs back depending on tube orientation, placing puffs at the back of the carpus and elbow, plus adding a cuff accent near the leg's cropped section before starting the tail sweep.

Writing shading paints and scale textures...

Good, that gives cream above the edge on the front. For the head I'm using position-based fur edges to separate jade from cream by height, and for the legs I'm banding the coat color transitioning into navy toward the lower section.

Moving to details: chest/belly cream, rump jade, then adding pendant discs as small torus shapes placed via surface rays, with tassels as downward spikes and gold bead spheres attached beneath them.

Now placing flank medallions and shoulder scroll plates using precise surface raycasts to find exact hit points and orient the geometry along the body's curvature.

I'll use the actual joint object for spine, adding more scroll shapes near the back and hips, plus mane extending around the tail. I'm also planning a dorsal ridge of small gold cones swept along the body from rump to chest, using a spike helper for each one.

Now I'm working out the body loft path between hip and spine joints, making sure the hip joint is created first as the root, and keeping the hooves as the lowest point so nothing clips the floor. I'm also adding extra cream puff shapes near the forehead, behind the antlers.

I need to be careful with unused imports since TypeScript treats them as errors, so I'm trimming the import list down to only what's actually used—builder, frame, offset, rng, catmull, limb, countershade, scales, cel, furEdge, and the SVG/glow helpers. Starting to write the builder setup and a helper function for generating a spiral path for cloud shapes...

Writing SVG swirl and cloud-tuft generation code...

Still defining more joints...

Still writing antler geometry...
